passages.note: Senate Third Reading vote page: Marsh is recorded No on the omnibus taxation bill, 16-14.

passages.provision_quote: 9. Subject to subsection F of this section, for taxable years beginning from and after December 31 of the year in which notice is provided to the department pursuant to section 43-243, subsection B, paragraph 2, the tax is 2.5% of taxable income.
passages.note: Bill text of the same instrument: beyond the income tax rate schedule it also rewrites unemployment insurance eligibility and benefits, class one property assessment ratios, urban revenue sharing, forest-products credits, school tuition organization rules and fire district levy limits.

rows.reasoning: The only record is Marsh's No vote on SB 1828 (2021), whose own title is "omnibus; taxation" and which amends unemployment insurance eligibility and benefit statutes, property tax assessment ratios, urban revenue sharing, income tax rates, several credits, school tuition organization rules and fire district levy limits. Under the vote ladder a No on a multi-subject bill proves nothing, because she may have objected to any part, so it cannot show whether she would "Moderately raise taxes on wealthy people and large companies to fund existing services" or "Keep the current tax system mostly as-is, with targeted adjustments — closing loopholes or granting narrow relief". No passage survives to support a chair.
